llm.summary: The skill mostly aligns with a local 'persona OS' that writes templates and runs shell helpers under ~/workspace, but there are notable inconsistencies and some areas you should review before installing (notably an undeclared dependency on the openclaw CLI and large executable scripts that will run via exec).

dimensions.detail: The name/description claim a local 'agent OS' that scaffolds files and optional cron jobs under ~/workspace; the included templates and scripts match that purpose. However, the runtime metadata and docs reference the openclaw CLI (openclaw cron add, openclaw gateway restart) and model flags (e.g., --model opus), but the skill's declared required binaries do not list the openclaw CLI or any gateway/tooling binary. Also the SKILL.md repeatedly asserts 'no network activity / no external API calls' while some templates reference using models and gateway/announce behavior that could imply networked actions if opted-in — this is an inconsistency to verify.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: SKILL.md is explicit: agent should operate only inside ~/workspace, prompt the user before overwriting files, and make cron/gateway changes opt-in. It instructs the agent to use exec to run shell commands and to follow a structured setup flow. There is no instruction in the provided content that directs reading system-wide sensitive files or exfiltrating secrets. That said, it enforces autonomous shell execution via exec (with user approval popups) and includes a large setup-wizard and scripts — review those scripts because the agent will be instructed to run them.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: No external download/install spec is provided (instruction-only), and all code files are bundled with the skill. This is lower risk than fetching arbitrary remote archives. There are no URLs or extract/install steps in the manifest to fetch external code at install time.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill requests no environment variables or credentials in its manifest, which is appropriate for a local workspace scaffolder. However, the templates include guidance for interacting with external services (Discord, Slack, using model flags) that would require separate credentials when/if the user enables those integrations. The skill does not declare or require those creds up front, but users should be prepared to supply them later if they opt into external features.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The skill declares it creates files under ~/workspace/ and may optionally schedule cron jobs via the openclaw CLI. always:false and no declared requests to modify other skills or system-wide settings are present. Cron and gateway changes are opt-in per the SKILL.md. This level of persistence is proportionate to the stated purpose, but cron/gateway changes should only happen with explicit user consent.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance:
Before installing or running this skill, consider the following:

- Inspect the big scripts first (scripts/setup-wizard.sh, scripts/security-audit.sh and any other scripts in the package). They are executable shell code and the agent will be instructed to run them via the exec tool. Verify they do only what you expect.
- The SKILL.md references the openclaw CLI (openclaw cron add, openclaw gateway restart) but the skill's declared required binaries do not include openclaw. If you plan to use scheduled jobs or gateway changes, ensure the openclaw CLI is installed and review what the cron jobs will do before enabling them.
- The skill asserts 'no network activity' in normal use, but some templates mention models or announcements which may perform networked actions if you opt into them. Treat external integrations (Discord/Slack/gateway/model calls) as separate consent steps and provide credentials only when you explicitly enable those features.
- The skill strongly pushes using exec (agent-run shell commands). Make sure you read each exec approval dialog carefully; do not blindly approve a sequence of commands without understanding them.
- Backup any existing ~/workspace data before running the setup if you already have files there — the skill promises to ask before overwriting, but it's safest to have a copy.
- Check author/homepage reputation (jeffjhunter.com) and consider running the included security-audit script locally first to see what it reports.
- If you want lower risk, keep the skill restricted to read-only inspection of the templates (do not approve exec runs) until you've audited the scripts and confirmed behavior.

Overall: the package appears to implement what it claims, but the missing declared dependency (openclaw CLI) and the presence of large, executable scripts that will be run by the agent justify caution — review the code and opt-in actions before approving execution.
